subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency/throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@finpay.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode question (hosted vs dedicated)

Hi Neha / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — that was really helpful. A couple follow-ups from our side based on the conversation:

- Our primary requirements are predictable p99 latency for inference (target ~120ms or better for 256-token completions) and the ability to sustain bursts up to ~250 req/s for short periods.
- We care about data isolation and predictable cost, but not strict on-prem for now.
- Would like to understand whether Redwood Hosted API can meet p99 latency targets at our peak QPS, or if we should plan for a Dedicated capacity reservation.

Can you confirm:
1) What configuration (instance/GPU equivalent, concurrency, batching) you would recommend for hitting p99 ~120ms at 250 req/s?
2) Do you offer a short benchmark/pilot on Dedicated to validate tail latency?
3) Rough cost delta between Hosted usage and Dedicated reserved capacity for an expected steady-state of ~50 req/s and peaks to 250 req/s?

I've attached our simple perf summary (prod-infra-overview.pdf) and a short sample payload. Happy to jump on a quick tech sync if useful.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Turner
Head of Platform
FinPay

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode question (hosted vs dedicated)

Hi Sam — great questions, and thanks for the clear targets. Quick answers up front, followed by a proposed next-step plan.

Short answers:
- Hosted: great for fast time-to-value and variable usage. For p99 ~120ms at 256-token completions, Hosted can meet that for lower concurrency/use cases but may struggle with sustained peaks at 250 RPS depending on model choice and burst pattern.
- Dedicated: recommended when you need predictable tail latency and isolation at scale. With a properly sized reserved pool and warm KV cache, Dedicated gives deterministic performance and easier capacity planning.

What we need to finalize sizing:
- Model you want to run in production (our benchmark defaults to the 7B-13B class for comparison).
- Typical request size distribution (you mentioned many short contexts; a short histogram would help).
- Desired fallback policy (graceful degradation to a smaller model or queueing).

Proposed next steps (can complete in a week):
1) Tech sync (30m): align on model, input distribution, and test script — Dylan can run the bench. Proposed times: Mon 4/19 or Tue 4/20.
2) Pilot bench: Redwood runs a dedicated pilot (best-effort reserved capacity) to reproduce p99 numbers with your payload. We provide the benchmark script and share raw numbers (we usually include p50/p95/p99 and token-level breakdown).
3) Draft SOW and cost comparison: I will send a draft SOW and an estimated Hosted vs Dedicated cost delta for steady-state 50 RPS with 250 RPS peaks.

I'll attach a short checklist and sample benchmark script. If that plan sounds good, I can slot Dylan to run the pilot the week of 4/26.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Neha — thanks, that plan works. Quick details to help sizing:

- We plan to run model: open-llama-13b or similar (we're evaluating both 7B and 13B variants).
- Request size: median completion length ~120 tokens, median context ~40 tokens.
- Traffic profile: steady-state ~50 RPS (business hours), short peaks up to 250 RPS for 10-20 minute windows (customer notification bursts).
- Budget: cost sensitivity matters — we want to avoid significant overprovisioning.

Two clarifying questions:
1) For Dedicated, do you warm KV caches automatically for frequent prefixes, or do we need an explicit caching layer?
2) Can you guarantee the pilot will include p99 tail measurements including cold-start behavior and steady-state? We're most concerned about warm steady-state p99 during burst events.

If helpful, we can provide a small sample traffic trace and a handful of production requests for the bench. Let me know if Dylan needs anything else.

—Sam

Sam — thanks for the details and for the sample profile. Finalizing next steps and deliverables below.

Planned deliverables:
- Dedicated pilot run (week of 4/26): Dylan will provision a small reserved pool configured to approximate a 4 x A100-equivalent capacity. The pilot will run your sample trace and a synthetic burst to 300 RPS for 15 minutes to validate steady-state and burst p99. We will collect p50/p95/p99, token breakdown, and GPU utilization.
- Benchmark scope: warm steady-state measurements + one cold-start run. We will mark results separately.
- SOW & cost comparison: attached SOW-draft-v1.pdf and a Hosted vs Dedicated delta for expected steady-state 50 RPS / peaks to 250 RPS.

Answers to your questions:
1) KV cache warmup: Dedicated supports automatic prefix/KV caching; we recommend priming the cache during the pilot to reflect production patterns. We also provide guidance on TTL/config for typical customer workloads.
2) Pilot p99 measurements: yes — the pilot will include both cold-start and warm steady-state p99 measurements. We'll highlight tail behavior during burst windows specifically.

Next actions for you: please send the sample traffic trace (or confirm you want us to replay the sample payload you attached earlier) and sign the attached SOW (or provide redlines). If you approve, I'll schedule the Dylan-led bench for Tue 4/27 10:00 AM PT.

Thanks — looking forward to validating this for you.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
